newsitem.title: USA: Alliance's sale of Red Ant sale falls through.
newsitem.headline: Alliance's sale of Red Ant sale falls through.

text.p: Alliance Entertainment Corp., the music distributor in bankruptcy proceedings, said it scrapped the planned sale of its Red Ant Records unit after unsecured creditors objected to the price.

Alliance had announced last week that it would sell Red Ant for $625,000 to venture capital firm Wasserstein Perella and retain a 10 percent share. Red Ant was founded last year by former MCA Music Entertainment Chairman Al Teller with a reported $20 million backing from Wasserstein Perella.
At a bankruptcy court hearing Wednesday to consider the deal, a committee of 11 unsecured creditors said the price was too low, Alliance said late Thursday.

Alliance and 14 of its subsidiaries filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection from creditors on July 14. Red Ant, based in Los Angeles, was not included in the filing. In Chapter 11 a company is protected from its creditors as it tries to work out a plan to pay its debts.
Court documents show the unsecured creditors include United Parcel Service, Bankers Trust New York Corp., TDK Corp., and the Harry Fox Agency, which licenses music.

At the hearing, Alliance said an offer of $2.2 million for Red Ant was submitted by Bust-It Records, an independent label formed by rapper MC Hammer. But the offer was not considered because Bust-It could not show it could fund the deal, the company said.
Alliance said Red Ant would have to seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection "on an expedited basis" unless it receives "an acceptable offer." An Alliance spokeswoman declined to elaborate.

After founding Red Ant, Teller incorporated it into Alliance through a series of transactions. Alliance defaulted on its debts and sought bankruptcy protection and Teller resigned as chairman of Red Ant. He remains chairman of Alliance.
